While Parvovirus B19 IgM is pending, the diagnosis is clinically definitive per established criteria — the CDC and pediatric dermatology literature recognize the triad of (1) preceding mild illness, (2) lacy reticular rash, and (3) absence of systemic signs as sufficient for clinical diagnosis in typical settings. No higher-priority organic or emergent condition is suggested by the data.
